items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states the equivalence of five descriptions of a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space: the definition, being the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological algebra with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, with one given by a sequence of weak ideals of definition, with one given by a sequence of ideals whose successive quotients are locally nilpotent, and finally being the formal spectrum of a limit of quotients of an algebra by such a sequence (statement lines 2492-2513). The proof first derives every other description from the definition: the space is the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible algebra by an earlier lemma on the types of affine formal algebraic spaces, and any presentation as a filtered colimit gives the algebra as the limit of its quotients by weak ideals of definition, which by a further earlier lemma form a countable fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of zero (proof lines 2515-2534). The converse direction from the last description is an argument about nilpotence: an element of the algebra dying in the first quotient has a power dying in the second because its image there is nilpotent, and so on inductively, so the kernel of the first projection is a weak ideal of definition and the algebra is weakly admissible (proof lines 2536-2549). Two of the remaining descriptions are immediate special cases, and the final step closes the cycle: from a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods one chooses open ideals inside them and intersects with a weak ideal of definition, obtaining a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition and hence a presentation of the space as a colimit (proof lines 2551-2565). The claim is H2: four implications are proved and each of them is a short but real manipulation, one of them an induction on the successive quotients in a filtered system of nilpotent ideals.
